A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVDD research, with matching authors, core algorithms, and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 Section 6 and Appendix C report original generation experiments for images, molecules, enhancers, and RNA, including reward comparisons, training curves, and an ablation.

after.justification: v4 Section 7 and Appendices B and F report original reward comparisons, molecular docking experiments, diversity and validity evaluations, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The core SVDD sampling procedure and MC/PM value estimators remain intact. Appendix D and Algorithm 5 add an optional arbitrary-proposal extension: candidates can come from q rather than the pretrained policy, with importance weights corrected by the pretrained-policy-to-q density ratio.

E1.justification: v4 adds molecular docking optimization against Parp1, 5ht1b, Jak2, and Braf using QuickVina 2. It removes the RNA-stability evaluation associated with Agarwal and Kelley, retaining RNA MRL, enhancer activity, image rewards, and molecular QED/SA. These change the evaluated task requirements, not merely dataset labels.

E2.justification: SMC becomes an evaluated comparator across the retained tasks in Table 2 and in a dedicated diversity comparison. In v1, its algorithm appeared only as an appendix extension without comparative results. Pretrained sampling, Best-of-N, and DPS remain; v4 also describes discrete DPS as combined with Nisonoff et al.'s guidance. DiGress is discussed but explicitly not empirically compared.

E3.justification: Table 2 replaces the 20% quantile with the 50% quantile while retaining the 10% quantile. New evaluation designs include validity and distributional metrics on 512 molecules per method, runtime/memory measurements, and expanded M sweeps. The principal pretrained models, denoising-step counts, and default SVDD settings remain unchanged; newly disclosed tuning details do not establish changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v4 expands the original aesthetic-score M ablation to include molecular QED, image compressibility, runtime, and memory. It adds an SMC-versus-SVDD diversity case study and quantitative molecular validity, novelty, and stability analyses. The existing MRL and enhancer training curves are retained with corrected captions; the RNA-stability curve is replaced by a docking-value-model curve.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 reports point estimates, whereas v4 Table 2 adds stated 95% confidence intervals. Neither version explains interval construction or provides seed or repeated-run counts. This establishes added uncertainty reporting, without establishing additional experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: v4 adds docking, SMC, image SVDD-MC, validity, and computational results, while removing RNA-stability and 20% quantile entries. Retained numerical entries also change: enhancer top-10 values for SVDD-MC and SVDD-PM change from 5.75 and 7.02 to 5.639 and 6.980. Several image and molecular values are retained or merely rounded; the revision does not establish a uniform same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix C introduces a discrete-guidance rate-matrix formulation and an informal asymptotic-equivalence derivation connecting Nisonoff et al.'s formulation to Theorem 1. The original target distribution, central theorem, SMC weight derivation, and soft-Q-learning identities are retained. Suppressing conditional notation while explicitly retaining conditional applicability is not a substantive theoretical change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claim: SVDD optimizes rewards in continuous and discrete pretrained diffusion models without differentiable proxy models or generative-model fine-tuning. Naming docking objectives in v4 makes the empirical support more specific without replacing this central contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantial explanations of SMC diversity loss, batch-size dependence, parallelization, and approximation-error propagation. It replaces v1's categorical naturalness assurance with more qualified discussion and empirical validity evidence. Appendix F also acknowledges that learned rewards can still require over-optimization controls, which are not implemented.

D1.justification: Appendix F substantially expands v1's sparse implementation information with network architectures, hyperparameter search ranges, dataset sizes and sequence lengths, image prompts, docking settings, software, and hardware. These mostly document settings rather than establish changed implementations. Hardware reporting is internally inconsistent: F.1.2 specifies A100 GPUs, while F.2 specifies RTX 2080Ti or A6000. The code-access link is retained.

R1.justification: v4 substantially revises the relationship to prior sampling research. It identifies SVDD as an instantiation of nested-IS SMC, adds Naesseth and diffusion-SMC references, and recasts v1's particle-filter extension as a comparison with existing methods. Section 6 and Appendices B/C also develop distinctions from standard SMC, discrete guidance, and DiGress.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory exposition receive wording edits, conditional notation is simplified, and extensions and limitations are reordered. Autoregressive related work moves to Appendix A, and experimental details gain clearer subdivisions. These are localized editorial and organizational changes within the retained problem-method-experiments narrative.

P2.justification: The expanded quantitative table moves from the appendix into the main results, while reward-distribution plots move to the appendix and gain panels. v4 adds SMC-diversity displays, molecular-validity Table 3, resource plots, and docking visualizations, and expands image examples across M values. It also corrects mislabeled training-curve captions and reorganizes the ablation into multiple panels.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important weaknesses in v1: missing evaluation against closely related SMC methods, incomplete attribution to that literature, and little quantitative evidence about naturalness or computational cost. The added comparisons, validity measurements, docking experiments, and implementation details substantially strengthen assessment of the central contribution. Removing RNA stability narrows coverage, and unexplained confidence intervals plus contradictory hardware and Figure 3 resource descriptions remain weaknesses, but they do not outweigh these gains.
